source.reason: Describes the near-rapid solidification (centrifugal casting) production of the as-cast 9Cr strip; the as-cast state is the un-annealed terminal condition, so no further heat treatment step applies to this sample.

method.value: centrifugal casting under near-rapid solidification (liquid metal poured into a copper mold at a rotating speed of 600 r/min)

processing_steps_notes.value: An alloy ingot made from high purity Fe/Mn/Al/C/Cr was reheated to melt by an induction coil, then the liquid metal was poured into a copper mold at a rotating speed of 600 r/min in Ar atmosphere; the obtained strip size was (60–80) mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm. This as-cast terminal state received no post-solidification heat treatment (annealing at 550 °C for 5 h applies to separate annealed samples).

source.reason: XRD (Fig.1) and OM (Fig.2) show as-cast strips are austenite+ferrite, more ferrite with higher Cr; quantitative ferrite fraction and austenite lattice constant for 9Cr are given in text; TEM (Fig.4, Fig.5) gives the dislocations, absence of κ-carbide, formation of Cr23C6 at grain boundaries (cubic, a=1.054 nm, width ~100 nm) and nano-scale DO3 in ferrite for the 9Cr strip.

overall_structure.value: Two-phase austenite (γ) + δ-ferrite; austenite is the major matrix phase and δ-ferrite uniformly distributes in the austenite matrix. Cr addition promotes ferrite (δ(110) intensity increases). No κ-carbide superlattice in the austenite of 9Cr; instead Cr23C6 carbides form at austenite grain boundaries, and nano-scale DO3 phase appears in the ferrite.

number_of_phases.value: 2 main phases (austenite γ + ferrite δ), plus Cr23C6 carbide at austenite grain boundaries and DO3 ordered phase in ferrite

morphology.value: granular or banded, located at austenite grain boundaries

dislocation_density.value: very high, but slightly lower than that of the 6Cr strip (no κ-carbide superlattice in SADP)

distribution.value: suppressed; no κ-carbide superlattice observed in austenite SADP of the as-cast 9Cr strip

source.reason: Combines phase-evolution/solidification-mode statement and the Cr-dependent suppression of κ-carbides with the appearance of grain-boundary Cr23C6 in the 9Cr strip.
The Cr23C6/grain-boundary cracking explanation for the poor ductility of the 9Cr strip is given in the discussion of as-cast 9Cr TEM (Fig. 4f) and the conclusions.

interaction_type.value: intergranular cracking along grain-boundary Cr23C6 carbides

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Cr23C6 carbides in granular or banded shapes with a width of about 100 nm at austenite grain boundaries may lead to inter-granular cracking along coarsening carbides at the grain boundary; formation of Cr23C6 carbides at austenite grain boundaries is a reason for the lowest ductility of as-cast and annealed 9 wt% Cr strips.

source.reason: Explanation given for the lower plasticity of Cr-containing as-cast strips, of which the 9Cr strip has the highest ferrite fraction (19.6 vol%).

interaction_type.value: δ-ferrite/austenite phase interfaces block dislocation propagation

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Increase of δ-ferrite fraction in Cr-containing strips blocks dislocation propagation due to more phase-interface areas, which may decrease the plasticity.

phase_evolution.value: Under near-rapid solidification, δ-ferrite first nucleated and grew from the melt (FA solidification mode: L → L+δ → L+δ+γ → δ+γ). With Cr addition the ferrite (δ) fraction increases and κ-carbide precipitation is suppressed; at 9 wt% Cr, Cr23C6 carbides form at austenite grain boundaries instead of κ-carbides.

interface_notes.value: The 9Cr strip shows the largest ferrite contribution (strongest δ-related XRD reflections) and forms Cr23C6 at austenite grain boundaries; no κ-carbide superlattice is observed in its austenite SADP.

unmapped_findings: For the as-cast 9Cr strip, addition of 9 wt% Cr suppresses κ-carbide precipitation in austenite (no κ-carbide superlattice in the SADP) and instead Cr23C6 carbides precipitate at austenite grain boundaries, which is stated to be the main reason for the lowest ductility and high strain hardening rate of as-cast (and annealed) 9Cr strips.

The dislocation density in the austenite of the as-cast 9Cr strip is still very high but slightly lower than that of the 6Cr strip; the solubility-related effect of 9 wt% Cr (higher solid solubility of C, Cr23C6 precipitation) is cited to reduce dislocation formation relative to 3Cr/6Cr.
The as-cast strip is reported to be almost free of casting defects due to the higher feeding capacity of the melt under great centrifugal force, with any present casting defects randomly distributed.

Slip-band spacing/width statistics after tensile fracture (Fig. 12, Fig. 13) were measured only for the 0Cr and 6Cr strips (as-cast 0Cr ~90 nm spacing / 13.4 nm width; as-cast 6Cr ~80 nm spacing / 12.5 nm width), so no slip-band values are reported for the 9Cr as-cast strip.
